name: Îles de Los
subtitle: The Îles de Los lie a few kilometres off Conakry.

facts.label: Islands
facts.value: Three main islands (Kassa, Roume, Tamara) and uninhabited islets (Cabri, Blanche, Corail, Fousset)

facts.label: Slave trade
facts.value: Used as a slave depot until the 1840s

facts.label: British fort
facts.value: Ruins of a fort built by the British in the early 19th century, from which operations against slave ships were launched

facts.label: Roume renamed
facts.value: Crawford Island was renamed after Ernest Roume when handed to France in 1904

facts.label: Kassa
facts.value: The British called it Factory Island

parts.text: The Îles de Los lie a few kilometres off Conakry. The archipelago has three main islands, Kassa, Roume and Tamara, and several uninhabited islets. Jeune Afrique says it passed under British (1818-1904) then French (1904-1958) rule and served as a slave depot until the 1840s.
